summary: DB2ERR is the shared DB2 SQL Error Handler subroutine. Called with a function code, it either LOGs a SQL error to the ERRLOG DB2 table (classifying severity and whether the error is retryable), DIAGnoses a SQLCODE into a human message + return code, or RETRieves the most recent logged error for a program. It recognises the common SQLCODEs (deadlock -911, timeout -913, connection -30081, duplicate key -803, not-found +100) and decides retry vs no-retry. It is the central SQL-error classification service that DB2CMT and other DB2 programs call.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SELECT CASE function
  WHEN 'LOG ': CALL 1000-LOG-ERROR
  WHEN 'DIAG': CALL 2000-DIAGNOSE-ERROR
  WHEN 'RETR': CALL 3000-RETRIEVE-ERROR
  ELSE: SET error; CALL 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE
END SELECT
RETURN (GOBACK)

paragraphs.name: 1000-LOG-ERROR
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CLEAR WS-ERRLOG-REC
ACCEPT timestamp
SET error-log fields: timestamp, program, type='D'
CALL 1100-SET-SEVERITY
Build EL-ERROR-CODE = CONCATENATE 'SQLCODE: ' + formatted sqlcode + ' STATE: ' + sqlstate
SET message, process date/time (from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE), user, additional info
CALL 1200-INSERT-ERROR

annotations.note: STRING builds a combined 'SQLCODE: nnn STATE: sssss' code string via COBOL STRING concatenation.

paragraphs.name: 1100-SET-SEVERITY
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SELECT CASE SQLCODE
  WHEN deadlock(-911) or timeout(-913): severity=2, SET should-retry
  WHEN connection(-30081): severity=4, no-retry
  WHEN dup-key(-803): severity=1, no-retry
  WHEN not-found(+100): severity=1, no-retry
  ELSE: IF sqlcode<0 THEN severity=3 no-retry ELSE severity=1 no-retry END IF
END SELECT
branches: EVALUATE SQLCODE: deadlock/timeout / connection / dup-key / not-found / other(+/-)

annotations.note: Business rule: only deadlock/timeout are retryable; everything else is no-retry. This drives caller retry logic.

paragraphs.name: 1200-INSERT-ERROR
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SQL INSERT INTO ERRLOG VALUES (:WS-ERRLOG-REC)
IF SQLCODE = 0 THEN SET LS-RETURN-CODE = 0
ELSE SET error 'Error logging to ERRLOG'; CALL 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE END IF
branches: IF insert SQLCODE=0 -> ok else error

annotations.note: Logs a DB2 error into a DB2 table — if that INSERT itself fails, it falls back to ERRPROC (file log), avoiding an infinite loop.

paragraphs.name: 2000-DIAGNOSE-ERROR
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SELECT CASE SQLCODE
  WHEN deadlock: text 'Deadlock detected - retry', rc=4
  WHEN timeout: text 'Timeout - retry', rc=4
  WHEN connection: text 'DB2 connection error', rc=12
  WHEN dup-key: text 'Duplicate key violation', rc=8
  ELSE: IF sqlcode<0 THEN 'Unhandled DB2 error', rc=12 ELSE 'DB2 warning condition', rc=4 END IF
END SELECT
paragraphs.notes: Maps a SQLCODE to a plain message + severity return code for the caller.

paragraphs.name: 3000-RETRIEVE-ERROR
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SQL SELECT error_message, error_severity, additional_info INTO :host vars
  FROM ERRLOG WHERE program_id = :LS-PROGRAM-ID AND error_timestamp = (latest for that program)
IF SQLCODE = 0 THEN return the message + severity
ELSE SET 'No error history found'; rc=4 END IF
branches: IF retrieve SQLCODE=0 -> return latest else 'no history'

annotations.note: Correlated subquery: fetches the most recent (MAX timestamp) logged error for the program.

paragraphs.name: 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE
paragraphs.pseudocode: SET ERR-PROGRAM = 'DB2ERR'; SET LS-RETURN-CODE = 12; CALL 'ERRPROC' PASSING ERR-MESSAGE

usage.note: Produced by Claude Code in-session; no API call, no key, no token cost.
